summary: Iteration 13: Driver phone+PIN login, driver authorization, admin PIN management and merchant problem alerts (failed / late / delivered_late) tested end-to-end. Backend: new suite 17/17 pass (after a test-side body fix for badges/seen) + full regression 140/140 pass (after updating the known-outdated test in test_admin_gating_weekly_email.py). 3 REAL emails were sent through Resend to delivered@resend.dev (failed, late, delivered_late), each with an email_id; alerts-off logs status 'off' with no recipients; repeat fail -> 400 and no second alert; late fires once only and blocks a later delivered_late. Frontend: driver sign-in (wrong PIN error + PIN cleared, correct login -> /driver/drv-1), redirects from /driver/drv-2, /driver/summary/drv-2 and /driver to own manifest, stop screen, PoD photo upload, scan screen (wrong-code error), complete drop, summary and sign-out all work. Admin /admin/drivers PIN reset works (weak-PIN red toast, success green toast); admin can open the /driver picker and drv-2. Merchant problem-alerts card shows the switch and the recent alerts list. Minor issues: tapping the Switch sends 2 PUTs, the PIN SAVE button overflows on mobile, a foreign stop shows a spinner for about 7s before the 403 error (react-query retries), and admin reset does not clear merchant_alerts. No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch) were found.

minor.issue: seed(force=True) wipes stops/orders but not db.merchant_alerts, so the merchant console keeps listing alerts for orders that no longer exist (seen: 4 TEST_Alert* entries are still there after a reset).

The 'running late' check only runs inside broadcast_route (a location ping, simulate-step, arrive, deliver or fail). Nothing checks on a timer, so if the driver app is paused or in the background, or the driver sits at one stop for a long time, the late email only goes out at the next driver action. It can arrive after the window has already passed.

Lockout design risk: 'drvip:{ip}' has a cap of 30 per IP and a successful login does not clear it, plus 'drv:{phone}:*' has a cap of 10 from anywhere. Drivers who share a depot NAT IP can all be locked out for 15 min after 30 bad tries in total, and anyone who knows a driver's phone number can lock that driver out. Consider an admin unlock flow (PIN reset already clears the per-phone keys but not the IP key).

ui_bugs.issue: The Switch sits inside a Pressable that also toggles. On web, one click on the Switch fires both onValueChange and the parent onPress, which sends 2 PUT /merchants/mer-1/alerts requests and 2 toasts (verified: PUT count 2 after one switch click). The 2 requests send the same value, so the result is correct but the call is duplicated. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ProblemAlertsCard.tsx:45-50

integration_issues.flow: Driver opens a stop on another driver's route
integration_issues.issue: The default QueryClient retries the 403 three times, so the stop screen shows a spinner for about 7s before 'ERR: This stop is on another driver's route'. Set retry so it skips 401/403/404 (src/query-client.ts:7).

issues: While editing a PIN, the SAVE button (driver-pin-save-<id>) has its right edge at x=391 on a 390 viewport, so it overflows the 16px right padding. The web TextInput with flex:1 does not shrink; add minWidth: 0 to the input (app/admin/drivers.tsx:57). The input is 48px tall but the Btn is 56px, so the two do not line up. Tablet (768) looks fine.
The error banner and the SIGN IN button use the same brand red fill, so the error does not stand out from the main button (minor).

action_items: ProblemAlertsCard: make the row Pressable and the Switch stop triggering each other (e.g. drop onPress on the row or set the Switch pointerEvents) so one tap sends one PUT.
admin/drivers.tsx: add minWidth: 0 to the PIN input (or flexShrink) and match its height to the SAVE Btn (56) so SAVE stays inside the padding on 390px screens.
query-client: retry: (n, err) => !/401|403|404/.test(status) && n < 2, so access-denied screens appear right away.
Admin reset: also run db.merchant_alerts.delete_many({}) in seed(force=True).
Optional: add a periodic background check (e.g. every minute for active routes today) that calls maybe_late_alerts, so 'running late' emails do not depend on driver pings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2884 lines, well over the 700-line guideline; split it into routers (auth, drivers, stops, merchants, alerts).

Authorization dependencies (require_driver_self / require_route_driver / require_stop_driver / ANY_DRIVER) are applied consistently. Admin passes all of them, and unassigned or foreign stops return 403 for drivers.
The driver login response and /auth/me never expose pin_hash. Wrong PIN and unknown phone return the same 401 message, and the dummy-hash check keeps timing similar.
Fail and late alerts are claimed with atomic update_one filters (merchant_fail_alert_at / merchant_late_alert_at = None), so they cannot be sent twice; verified.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_admin_gating_weekly_email.py (ids fixture now uses the admin token for GET /routes/{id}; the open-endpoints check now only covers /track)

The alert tests in test_driver_login_merchant_alerts.py send 3 REAL emails; deselect TestMerchantAlerts (and send_now) in regression runs to save the email quota. rca_of_issue: Switch double PUT: Switch onValueChange and the parent Pressable onPress both call toggle() because the web click bubbles up. Spinner delay: the react-query default of retry=3 with exponential backoff also applies to 403. SAVE overflow: on web, the TextInput with flex:1 keeps its intrinsic minimum width.
